title: Deep Learning Architectures
learning_outcomes: Explain deep Learning Architectures and connect at least two of its listed subtopics.
Apply the central idea in deep Learning Architectures to a small example or select a suitable approach for a stated scenario.
Identify an important assumption, failure mode, risk, or limitation and describe how it should be checked.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study deep Learning Architectures within Neural Networks and Deep Learning. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Neural networks are parameterized functions trained by optimizing a loss. Small, inspectable experiments help reveal how data, gradients, and settings interact.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Architectures encode structural assumptions about input and dependency patterns. Convolutions, recurrent units, attention, and transformers support different use cases, but suitability still depends on data, cost, and evaluation.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics covered in this lesson

items.title: Feedforward networks
items.text: Feedforward networks is one of the concepts used to reason about deep learning architectures. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Convolutional neural networks
items.text: Convolutional neural networks use local filters and shared weights to process spatial patterns in image-like data. Input dimensions, stride, padding, and label quality affect the learned representation.

items.title: Recurrent neural networks
items.text: Recurrent models process sequences while carrying a hidden state from one step to the next. Sequence length, state behavior, training stability, and the task’s temporal structure are important considerations.

items.title: Long short-term memory networks
items.text: Recurrent models process sequences while carrying a hidden state from one step to the next. Sequence length, state behavior, training stability, and the task’s temporal structure are important considerations.

items.title: Gated recurrent units
items.text: Recurrent models process sequences while carrying a hidden state from one step to the next. Sequence length, state behavior, training stability, and the task’s temporal structure are important considerations.

items.title: Attention mechanisms
items.text: Attention combines information from sequence positions according to learned compatibility scores. Transformer architectures use attention and other components to model context; context length and compute costs remain practical constraints.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Identify what deep learning architectures takes as input and what result or decision it is intended to support. 2. Read the example before running it and predict the output. 3. Run the small example, compare actual and expected output, then change one input or assumption and repeat. 4. content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. Neural networks are parameterized functions trained by optimizing a loss. Small, inspectable experiments help reveal how data, gradients, and settings interact.

content_blocks.code:
inputs = [0.5, 1.0]
weights = [2.0, -1.0]
bias = 0.25
score = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(inputs, weights)) + bias
relu = max(0.0, score)
print("score:", round(score, 2))
print("relu:", round(relu, 2))

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. If the example runs as expected, do not infer that it proves a trained model works; this snippet is a deterministic teaching aid. Keep sensitive data out of tests.

content_blocks.title: Check before you trust a result
content_blocks.text: This is a small, deterministic teaching example—not a trained AI model or evidence of production performance. Run it with a local Python 3 interpreter; do not paste secrets or private data into experiments.
